clue.text: How Red Arrows fly — low-down

definitions.meaning: the RAF display team flies in tight formation, read here as two words
low-down is slang for the inside facts or details

explanation.walkthrough: The Red Arrows are the Royal Air Force's aerobatic display team, famous for flying in close formation.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it describes flying in formation; as one word it is a synonym for the inside facts.

clue.text: From Orion a direction opposite the zenith

indicators.note: From says the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: An astronomer takes a bearing from the constellation Orion.
explanation.walkthrough: The starry surface makes 'Orion' look like part of the picture, but its last letter starts the run.
explanation.definitionFit: The lowest point of the celestial sphere lies directly below the observer, the exact opposite of the zenith.

clue.text: Supervise some poetry in Old English

indicators.note: in places the poetry inside the abbreviation for the old language

parts.note: verse is poetry, or some lines of it

explanation.surface: An instruction to supervise the study of poems written in Old English.
explanation.definitionFit: To supervise work is to watch over and direct it, a straight synonym.

clue.text: SF movie in original art mix

indicators.note: original suggests a fresh, inventive arrangement of the letters that follow

explanation.surface: A science-fiction film described as an original mixture of art styles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'original' poses as praise for the film; it signals the rearrangement of ART MIX.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1999 Wachowski science-fiction film starring Keanu Reeves is called The Matrix.

clue.text: Mrs Simpson allowed to set up message

indicators.note: in a down clue set up means the pieces are read upwards, that is backwards

parts.note: Marge is Mrs Simpson in the cartoon The Simpsons
let means allowed

explanation.surface: Mrs Simpson was permitted to arrange a message to be sent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mrs Simpson' may suggest Wallis Simpson, but it is Marge of the cartoon; 'set up' turns MARGE LET into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A telegraphed communication is a kind of written message, so the general word defines it.

clue.text: Watch start of tennis game following outside broadcast

indicators.note: following places the tennis term after the broadcasting abbreviation

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for an outside broadcast, television made away from the studio
every point in tennis begins with a serve

explanation.surface: A viewer watches the opening of a tennis match on an outside broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start of' looks like a first-letter pick, but the whole phrase means the serve that opens play.
explanation.definitionFit: To observe something is to watch it attentively, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Fixed seat with unsound piece of wood having got men in

parts.note: rotten means unsound or decayed

indicators.note: having got with in says the wood takes the soldiers inside it
in completes the container signal, the men going into the wood

parts.note: a bough is a large branch of a tree
OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers or men

explanation.surface: A rickety seat made of decayed wood, with workmen fitted inside.
explanation.walkthrough: A rotten borough was a pre-1832 British parliamentary constituency with almost no voters, whose seat was effectively fixed by a patron.
explanation.definitionFit: Such a constituency returned its member by arrangement, so its seat was effectively fixed in advance.

clue.text: To have casual affairs outside Middle Eastern country is sensible

indicators.note: outside puts the word for sensible around the country

parts.note: wise means sensible
Oman is a country in the Middle East

explanation.surface: Advice that seeking flings abroad in the Middle East is prudent.
explanation.definitionFit: To womanise is to pursue many casual sexual relationships with women, matching the infinitive phrase.

clue.text: Make up glamorised tot — one may improve complexion

indicators.note: make up means put together, so the letters are assembled anew

explanation.surface: Instructions to apply cosmetics to a toddler already made glamorous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make up' reads as cosmetics; it is the rearrangement signal for GLAMORISED TOT.
explanation.definitionFit: A skin specialist treats conditions of the skin, so such a doctor may improve someone's complexion.

clue.text: Veteran man fighting endlessly

indicators.note: endlessly means both end letters are removed from the word

parts.note: a soldier is a man who fights

explanation.surface: An old campaigner still battling on without end.
explanation.definitionFit: An oldie is an old person or thing, so a veteran in the general sense of long-serving.

clue.text: Cleese top comic in shower of stars

indicators.note: comic suggests the letters are played around with for laughs

explanation.surface: John Cleese, the top comedian, appears in a show of stars.
explanation.walkthrough: John Cleese is a British comedian of Monty Python fame; 'comic' signals the rearrangement of CLEESE TOP.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as one who shows, a shower of stars is an instrument that reveals stars to the eye.

clue.text: Get beating being reckless in affair

indicators.note: in puts the word for reckless inside the word for affair

parts.note: thing can mean an affair, as in having a thing with someone
rash means reckless

explanation.surface: Someone takes a hiding after behaving recklessly in a love affair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get' is a link: the wordplay gets the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A beating and a thrashing are both a physical punishment of repeated blows, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Domain of actual money

parts.note: real means actual
M is an abbreviation for money, as in economists' M1 and M3

explanation.surface: A question of where real money comes from.
explanation.definitionFit: A realm is a kingdom or sphere, the same as a domain.

clue.text: Two party leaders arrested

parts.note: Nick Clegg led the Liberal Democrats when the puzzle appeared
Ed Miliband led the Labour Party at the same time

explanation.surface: News that the heads of two political parties have been taken into custody.
explanation.walkthrough: In 2011 Nick Clegg led the Liberal Democrats and Ed Miliband led Labour; 'leaders' tempts a first-letter pick, but it is their first names.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicked is British slang for arrested by the police.

clue.text: Reputation applied to Devon town

parts.note: credit means good standing or reputation
on means applied, as a coat of paint is on

explanation.surface: A town in Devon gains a good name.
explanation.walkthrough: Crediton is a small town in Devon, a county in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Crediton is a market town in mid Devon, so this is an example of the class named.

clue.text: Piece of information about tool returned for renovation process

indicators.note: about puts the piece of information around the turned tool

parts.note: a fact is a piece of information

indicators.note: returned means the tool's name is read backwards

parts.note: a file is a tool for smoothing metal or wood

explanation.surface: A snippet of data about a tool sent back for refurbishment.
explanation.walkthrough: The tool is a file for smoothing wood or metal; 'returned' makes ELIF. A facelift is surgery favoured for renovating ageing looks, and the surface's refurbished tool is a red herring.
explanation.definitionFit: Cosmetic surgery that tightens the face is a renovation of one's looks, and the word is also used for refurbishing a building.

clue.text: Ace involved with shunt, not being restrained

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the letters are mixed together

explanation.surface: A top pilot caught up in a minor crash, behaving without restraint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link joining the two fodder words ACE and SHUNT, whose letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Unchaste means sexually unrestrained, so lacking restraint in that sense.

clue.text: Harmonic apparent on single

indicators.note: on places the first word upon the second, so it comes first in an across answer

parts.note: overt means open or apparent
one means single

explanation.surface: A harmony that shows up clearly on a pop single.
explanation.definitionFit: In acoustics a harmonic is a higher frequency sounding above the fundamental, which is exactly what an overtone is.

clue.text: Note French city's occupation at a price

parts.note: te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale
Nancy is a city in north-east France; the 's joins it on

explanation.surface: A remark that a French city's property is let for rent.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenancy is the occupation of property in return for rent, a paid-for occupation.

clue.text: Unpleasant time in gold trade

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry
a deal is a trade or transaction

explanation.surface: A rough patch for a dealer in the gold market.
explanation.definitionFit: An ordeal is a painful experience, so an unpleasant time to go through.

clue.text: Venomous creature hunting dog round lake

indicators.note: round says the dog's name goes around the abbreviation

parts.note: a ratter is a dog used for hunting rats
L is the abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: A dangerous animal stalked by a hound around a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: Rattler is informal for a rattlesnake.
explanation.definitionFit: A rattlesnake is a venomous viper, so the informal name names a venomous creature.

clue.text: Device to bind up hay without a motor initially

indicators.note: without says the letter named next is dropped

parts.note: to embale is to make hay into bales
the letter A as written

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A gadget for baling hay that works without an engine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without a' takes A out of EMBALE to leave EMBLE; 'initially' adds M from motor.
explanation.definitionFit: In heraldry a device is a symbolic design or badge, which is what an emblem is.

clue.text: Bulb working with charge carrier

parts.note: on means working, as a switched-on machine
an ion is an atom carrying an electric charge

explanation.surface: A light bulb switched on, with the current running.
explanation.definitionFit: The onion is a bulb vegetable, so it is an example of a bulb.

clue.text: It may be pulled running around top of Main Street

indicators.note: around puts the word for running about the street pieces

parts.note: haring means running fast, like a hare

indicators.note: top of picks the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A runner dashing round the top of Main Street pulls up injured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main Street' reads as one place name, but 'top of' takes only Main's first letter while Street stays the usual abbreviation; 'running' is haring, dashing like a hare.
explanation.definitionFit: A tendon at the back of the knee, which athletes often pull or strain.

clue.text: Cross sea-dog losing head

indicators.note: losing head means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: a sea-dog can be a pirate, a sea rover

explanation.surface: An old sailor angry after losing his captain.
explanation.definitionFit: Cross as an adjective means angry or annoyed, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Weed that's rampant under logs

indicators.note: rampant means growing wildly, so the letters run riot

explanation.surface: A weed that grows wild beneath piles of logs.
explanation.definitionFit: Groundsel is a common yellow-flowered garden weed.

clue.text: See trailers — perhaps with these

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning see or look
trailers are advertisements for coming films

explanation.surface: A request to look at the film trailers, perhaps with plenty of them.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: trailers, the towed kind, may be seen carrying these.
explanation.definitionFit: Trailers towed behind vehicles carry cargo, so they are seen with these burdens on board.

clue.text: Harry kept me working in very big shop

indicators.note: working means operating on, so the letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Harry has kept me employed in a huge store.
explanation.definitionFit: A hypermarket is a very large supermarket, usually out of town.
